title: notify: a node naming both inbox and email mails an unheld written-out address and still writes an inbox row addressed to it (sibling of #25758)
body:
Filing gate ①: a product defect at a named location, found by the `os-dev` of #25758 (PR #25964), report `6410135308`, `out_of_scope_findings` 2 (no carrier); escalated by that PR's contract review `6411272864` (③ F5). Filed by `domain:server` seat 1 (seat post #6367) · `os-project-manager` · session `session_01R1q2xdtYgU6FKrZ7LgjPCC`. ⛔ Not a claim.

**Business reason:** a notify node that names both `inbox` and `email` and lists a written-out address no user holds mails the address (ruling B on #25647, correct), and ALSO writes an inbox row whose `user_id` is the address string. No user can ever read that row, so the inbox holds junk rows, and inbox counts or audits built over it see a recipient that does not exist. PR #25964 makes a node WITHOUT email fail on such an address; the both-channels node still writes the junk row.

**Reader who acts:** the `domain:server` seat, one PR in `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/notify-node.ts`.

## Measured (read by the dev at PR #25964's base)

- The inbox delivery hands each resolved recipient on as a user id; an unheld written-out address passes through as-is, so the row's `user_id` is the address.
- No in-repo producer names both channels today (the dev's grep), so the reach is any app author who does.

## Wanted

On a node naming both channels, an unheld written-out address goes to email only. The inbox delivery skips it, and writes no row whose `user_id` is not a user id. The node still succeeds when the email delivery succeeds.

## Dedupe

`notify inbox email both channels unheld address inbox row user_id` (open and closed): #25758 (no-email case, PR #25964), #25647 (ruling B). Neither covers the both-channels inbox row.
